Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[4] "Say: Have you considered those you invoke besides Allah? Show me what they have created of the earth, or do they have a share in the heavens? Bring me a Book before this, or some remnant of knowledge, if you are truthful."

"Say: Have you considered those you invoke besides Allah?" i.e., the idols that you worship. "Show me what they have created of the earth, or do they have a share in the heavens?" i.e., show me what influence what you worship has over any earthly thing independently, or over any heavenly thing by partnership, such that it deserves to be worshipped. "Bring me a Book before this" is a rebuke to them, by their incapacity to produce a transmitted proof, after rebuking them for their incapacity to produce a rational proof. That is: bring me a divine Book from before this Qur'an, which articulates monotheism and the nullification of association, and which indicates the soundness of your religion. "Or some remnant of knowledge" i.e., or some remnant of knowledge that has survived from you of the sciences of the earlier peoples, bearing witness to their deserving worship. "If you are truthful" i.e., in your claim. For it can hardly be sound unless a rational proof or a transmitted authority stands behind it. Since neither of these stands behind it, while the proofs of reason and transmission stand against it, its falsehood becomes evident.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[5] ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than God those who will not answer him until the Day of Resurrection, while they are heedless of their calling?﴾

﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than God those who will not answer him﴾, meaning: his supplication, because of their incapacity to respond to it: ﴿until the Day of Resurrection, while they are heedless of their calling﴾, meaning: because they are either inanimate objects, or subjugated beings preoccupied with their own affairs. The word "heedlessness" (al-ghaflah) is a metaphor (majaz, figurative usage) for the absence of any benefit from them, or it is a case of predominance (taghlib, giving precedence to one category over another), where heedlessness is attributed to those who are capable of it over others.

A subtle point:

Al-Nasir said: In His saying ﴿until the Day of Resurrection﴾ there is a fine point. He made the Day of Resurrection the limit (ghayah, end-point) of non-response, and it is the nature of an end-point that the thing it limits comes to an end there. Yet the non-response continues after this limit, because on the Resurrection Day too they will not respond to them. The correct view, and God knows best, is that it is one of the end-points that indicate that what follows it, although it agrees with what precedes it, is in fact greater than it by a clear increase that places it in the second category, so much so that the two states, although they are of one type, are as opposites due to the difference between them. This is because the first state, whose limit is made the Resurrection, does not exceed non-response, whereas the second state, which is on the Resurrection Day, exceeds non-response by enmity and by disbelief in their worship of them. This belongs to the same category as what preceded a little earlier (p-٥٣٣٩) in Surat al-Zukhruf, in His saying: ﴿Rather, I gave enjoyment to these and their fathers until the truth and a clear messenger came to them﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 29] ﴿And when the truth came to them, they said, "This is magic, and we are disbelievers in it."﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 30]. End.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[6] ﴿And when mankind are gathered, they will be enemies to them, and they will be deniers of their worship.﴾

﴿And when mankind are gathered﴾ means: they are brought together on the Day of Resurrection to the place of reckoning. ﴿They will be﴾ means: their deities. ﴿Enemies to them﴾ means: because of their disavowal of them. Al-Shihab said: "Enemies" is a metaphor (isti'arah), or a sent metonymy (majaz mursal) for what harms. ﴿And they will be deniers of their worship﴾. Ibn Jarir said: that is, the deities they used to worship in the world will deny their worship, because they will say on the Day of Resurrection: "We did not command them to worship us, nor did we perceive their worship of us. We disown them before You, O our Lord!" So the denial is by way of speech, intending to make clear that what they truly worshipped was in reality the devils and their own desires.

Al-Qashani said: They will be enemies, because the worship of the people of this world for their masters and their service to them is only for a self-centred purpose. Likewise is the enslavement of masters to their servants. So when the purposes are removed and the causes and reasons cease, they will be enemies to them, and they will deny their worship, and they will say: "You did not serve us, but you served yourselves." As was said in the explanation of His words: ﴿The intimate friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the righteous﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 67]. End of quotation.

It was also said: the pronoun in "they will be" in both places refers to the worshippers, so that no disjunction arises. This is open to objection, because it contradicts what is apparent from the context, since the context is about describing the state of the deities with them, not the reverse. Also, their disbelief would then be a denial of their worship, and calling it "disbelief" is also contrary to the apparent meaning. This is made clear by the verses: ﴿And they have taken deities besides Allah that they may be for them a source of might﴾ [Maryam: 81], ﴿No! They will reject their worship and will become opponents to them﴾ [Maryam: 82]. The Qur'an explains one part of itself by another.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[7] ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieve say of the truth when it has come to them, "This is evident magic."﴾

﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieve say of the truth when it has come to them, "This is evident magic."﴾ That is, they confronted it with denial the moment they heard it, without any circulation of thought (*ijālat fikr*) or exercise of sight (*iʿmāl ru'yah*). The *lām* in "*lil-ḥaqq*" is the *lām al-ajal* (the *lām* of cause or purpose), governed by "*qāla*." It has also been said that it carries the meaning of the *bāʾ* (*bi-*, "against"), governed by "*kafarū*." Disbelief was made to take the *lām* by analogy with its opposite, which is belief, since belief is construed with it, as in His saying, ﴿Shall we believe you?﴾ (Surah al-Shuʿarāʾ, 26:111).

**The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[8] ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Say, "If I have invented it, then you cannot avail me anything against Allah. He is most knowing of what you spread into it. Sufficient is He as witness between me and you; and He is the Forgiving, the Merciful."﴾

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Say, "If I have invented it, then you cannot avail me anything against Allah"﴾ meaning: you cannot ward off from me any harm if He afflicts me with it. The "am" (أم) here, according to what they said, is *munqati'ah* (disjunctive) and is estimated to be equivalent to *bal* (rather), the transitional *idrab* (shift of statement), and the interrogative hamza, used figuratively to express denial and wonder. The reason fabrication is more heinous than sorcery, such that he turned away from it, is that lying, especially against Allah, is agreed to be ugly, so much so that you see everyone recoil from attributing it to Him. Sorcery, by contrast, though ugly, does not reach this degree, so that knowing it is almost counted among desirable qualities.

Al-Naasir said: This transition, in its category, is like the purpose I mentioned just before in its place, for it is a shift to something that agrees with the previous claim but is greater than it. Because of its addition over the first, together with what preceded it that falls short of it, it took the status of two contradictories, like negation and affirmation, one of which is turned away from in favor of the other. That is because their attributing the verses to being fabrications is more severe and further than attributing them to being sorcery. So he turned away from that first claim to what he mentioned, which is stranger than it. End of quotation.

﴿He is most knowing of what you spread into it﴾ meaning: you plunge into discussing His matter, whether it is sorcery or falsehood. ﴿Sufficient is He as witness between me and you﴾ meaning: He bears witness to my truthfulness by the signs with which He supports me and the truth of His promises. ﴿And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ meaning: toward whoever among you returns from disbelief, repents, and believes.

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[9] ﴿Say: "I am not an innovation among the messengers, nor do I know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow what is revealed to me, and I am but a clear warner."﴾

﴿Say: "I am not an innovation among the messengers"﴾ That is: I am not the first of the messengers of God whom He has sent to His creation. Many messengers came before me, sent to nations before you. So why do you deny my mission and find my message far-fetched? Compare His words: ﴿Muhammad is only a messenger; messengers have passed away before him﴾ [Al-Imran: 144]. And (bid') is like (badi'), meaning new and originated. Ibn Jarir said: Among the uses of (bid') is the verse of 'Adi ibn Zayd:

"So I am not an innovation among the events that befall men, whom ease and hardship have overtaken in turn."

(p-5342) And among the uses of (badi') is the verse of al-Ahwas:

"She boasted and then claimed kinship, so I said: 'Leave me! The ignorance you have been brought to is no novelty.'"

﴿Nor do I know what will be done with me or with you.﴾ Abu al-Su'ud said: That is, what will befall us of the events of time to come, from God's actions, and what He will decree for us of His judgments. It is related from al-Hasan, may God be pleased with him: "I do not know what my affair and your affair will come to in this world." It was also said: it is possible that what is negated is detailed knowledge. The more apparent view is that (ma) refers to what knowledge of which is not among the functions of prophethood, namely the worldly events and occurrences, not what will happen in the Hereafter, for knowledge of that is among the functions of prophethood, and revelation has come with it explicitly, detailing what will be done to both parties. End of quotation.

This more apparent view comes close to the saying of al-Hasan, and it is what Ibn Jarir relied upon. Ibn Kathir said: Rather, nothing else is permissible. How so? He ﷺ was certain that he would enter Paradise, he and those who followed him in goodness. As for this world, he did not know what his affair would lead to, nor the affair of the idolaters of Quraysh: would they believe, or would they disbelieve and be punished, and be uprooted for their disbelief. As for the hadith related by Imam Ahmad from Umm al-'Ala', who had pledged allegiance to the Prophet ﷺ, she said: ("When the Ansar cast lots for the dwelling of the emigrants, 'Uthman ibn Maz'un, may God be pleased with him, fell to our lot. 'Uthman fell ill with us, and we nursed him. When he died, we wrapped him in his garments, and the Messenger of God ﷺ entered upon us. I said: 'May God's mercy be upon you, Abu al-Sa'ib! My testimony for you is that God, Mighty and Majestic, has honored you.' The Messenger of God ﷺ said: 'As for him, certainty has come to him from his Lord, and I hope good for him. By God! I do not know, though I am the Messenger of God, what will be done with me!' She said: I said: 'By God! I will never again declare anyone pure after him,' and that grieved me. Then I slept, and I saw a flowing spring for 'Uthman, may God be pleased with him. I came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and informed him of that, and the Messenger of God ﷺ said: 'That is his deed.'") Al-Bukhari alone related it without Muslim, and in one of his wordings: "I do not know, though I am the Messenger of God ﷺ, what will be done with him." This is more likely to be the preserved version, as evidenced by her saying: "that grieved me." In this and similar reports there is an indication that no one specific is to be declared certain of Paradise, except those whom the Lawgiver explicitly named, such as the ten (given glad tidings of Paradise), Ibn Salam, al-'Umaysa', Bilal, Suraqa, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn Haram (the father of Jabir), the seventy reciters who were killed at Bi'r Ma'una, Zayd ibn Haritha, Ja'far, and Ibn Rawaha, and those like them, may God be pleased with them all. End of Ibn Kathir's words.

Al-Mahayimi said: ﴿Nor do I know what will be done with me or with you﴾ That is, concerning what has not been revealed to me. Revelation about some matters does not necessitate knowledge of the rest, and it was not for me to add to the revelation a lie of my own.

﴿I only follow﴾ That is, in establishing the unseen matters, ﴿what is revealed to me﴾. ﴿And I am but a clear warner﴾ That is, a warner of God's punishment for your disbelief in Him, who has made clear his warning to you, and made clear his call to what is good for you and your happiness.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[10] ﴿Say: "Have you considered? If it is from Allah, and you have disbelieved in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel has testified to the like of it and believed while you were arrogant—indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people."﴾

(p-5344) ﴿Say: "Have you considered? If it is from Allah"﴾ — that is, the Qur'an is sent down from Him to me, not magic nor fabrication as you claim. ﴿And you have disbelieved in it, and a witness from the Children of Israel﴾ — that is, from those who are acquainted with the secrets of revelation through what they were given of the Torah. ﴿Has testified to the like of it﴾ — that is, the like of the Qur'an, which is what is in the Torah of the rulings that confirm the Qur'an, including belief in Allah alone and what follows from it, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed it is in the Scriptures of the former peoples﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 196], and His saying: "Indeed, this is in the former scriptures, the scriptures of Abraham and Moses" [al-A'la: 18–19]. Or it is "upon the like of what has been mentioned," namely its being from Allah, exalted is He. Or "upon the like of the testimony of the Qur'an," so that his testimony that it is from Allah is made a testimony upon the like of the testimony of the Qur'an, since by its inimitability it is as if it testifies for itself that it is from Allah. Or "the like" (al-mithl) is a relative (silah) and the "fa'" in His saying ﴿and believed﴾ is for indicating that he hastened to believe in the Qur'an, because he knew that it is of the kind of revelation that speaks the truth. ﴿While you were arrogant﴾ — that is, from believing in it after this testimony.

As for His saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾, it is a resumptive clause (isti'naf) indicating that their disbelief is due to their misguidance, which is caused by their wrongdoing, and it is evidence for the omitted response (jawab), like: "Are you not wrongdoers?" or "Who is then more astray than you?" That is, non-guidance is something that indicates misguidance with certainty. So it is like His saying in the other verse: ﴿Say: "Have you considered? If it is from Allah, and you disbelieved in it, who is more astray than one who is in extreme opposition?"﴾ [Fussilat: 52].

Abu al-Su'ud said: He described them with wrongdoing to indicate the cause of the judgment, for His leaving them without guidance is due to their wrongdoing.

Note:

It is narrated that the witness is 'Abdullah ibn Salam, and so the verse would be Medinan and an exception within the surah, as al-Kawashi mentioned, because his Islam occurred in Medina. It was answered: there is no need for an exception, and the verse is of the type of informing before occurrence, like His saying: ﴿And the companions of the heights will call out﴾ [al-A'raf: 48]. What supports this is that "testified" (shahida) is coordinated with the condition by which the past tense becomes future, so there is no harm in the testimony of the witness (p-5345) after its revelation, and his being explained by it is a clarification of the actual event, not that it is specifically intended by it. This is what they verified. Much of what we mention regarding the purpose of the occasion of revelation in such cases is close to this, and that it is an illustration of what the noble expression encompasses.

Then he pointed to relating a kind of their falsehoods concerning the revelation and the believers in it, so he said, glorified is He:

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:**

[11] ﴿Those who disbelieved said of those who believed, "If it had been good, they would not have preceded us to it." And since they have not been guided by it, they will say, "This is an ancient lie."﴾

﴿Those who disbelieved said of those who believed, "If it had been⁠—"﴾ That is, faith, or what the Messenger brought. ﴿"...good, they would not have preceded us to it."﴾ That is: if it had come from Allah, we would have been more entitled to it, as with the other good things of wealth and status.

Ibn Kathir said: They meant Bilal, Ammar, Suhayb, Khabbab, may Allah be pleased with them, and those like them and their kind among the oppressed, the slaves and the female slaves. They thought this because they believed in themselves that they had standing with Allah and that He had special care for them. They erred in this with a gross error and a manifest mistake, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And thus We tested some of them through others, that they might say, "Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?"﴾ (Al-An'am: 53). That is, they wonder how these people were guided and not themselves. For this reason they said: ﴿"If it had been good, they would not have preceded us to it."﴾ As for the People of the Sunnah and the Community (Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah), they say of every action and statement that is not established from the Companions (Sahabah), may Allah be pleased with them, that it is an innovation (bid'ah, a newly introduced practice in religion), because if it were good, they would have preceded us to it, since they left out no aspect of good except that they hastened to it. End of quote.

﴿And since they have not been guided by it⁠—﴾ that is, by the Qur'an: ﴿they will say, "This is an ancient lie."﴾ That is, an old falsehood, as they said: "tales of the ancients."

Ibn Kathir said: So they belittle the Qur'an and its people. This is the arrogance of which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Rejecting the truth and looking down on people."

(p-5346)

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[12] ﴿And before it was the Book of Moses, an imam and a mercy. And this is a Book confirming it in the Arabic tongue, to warn those who have done wrong, and as good tidings to the good-doers.﴾

﴿And before it was the Book of Moses, an imam and a mercy﴾ means: a model (imam) to be followed in the religion of God and His laws, and a mercy for whoever believes in it and acts by what is in it. ﴿And this﴾, that is, the one about which they say what they say, ﴿is a Book confirming﴾, that is, confirming the Book of Moses without having learned it from the One who sent it down to him, ﴿in the Arabic tongue﴾, that is, clear and plain. In qualifying the Book by this, although its being in Arabic is a matter whose indication is well known, there is an implication that its confirmation of the Book of Moses lies in the unity of its meaning with it, while the Book of Moses is not in Arabic. Someone like this could not know that tongue except through revelation from God, exalted is He. ﴿To warn those who have done wrong, and as good tidings to the good-doers.﴾

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 46, verses 13–14:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[13–14] ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast – there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve. Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding eternally therein as a reward for what they used to do.﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 14].

﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah"﴾ i.e., (saying) that there is no other. ﴿Then remain steadfast﴾ i.e., upon righteous deeds. Al-Qadi (al-Baydawi) said: That is, they combined tawhid (monotheism), which is the essence of knowledge, with steadfastness in matters, which is the culmination of action. And "then" (thumma) indicates the delay of the rank of action and that its consideration depends upon tawhid. ﴿There will be no fear concerning them﴾ i.e., from the terror of the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Nor will they grieve﴾ i.e., the Great Terror will not grieve them. ﴿Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding eternally therein as a reward for what they used to do﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 14]

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 46, verses 13–14:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[13–14] ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast – there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve. Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding eternally therein as a reward for what they used to do.﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 14].

﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah"﴾ i.e., (saying) that there is no other. ﴿Then remain steadfast﴾ i.e., upon righteous deeds. Al-Qadi (al-Baydawi) said: That is, they combined tawhid (monotheism), which is the essence of knowledge, with steadfastness in matters, which is the culmination of action. And "then" (thumma) indicates the delay of the rank of action and that its consideration depends upon tawhid. ﴿There will be no fear concerning them﴾ i.e., from the terror of the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Nor will they grieve﴾ i.e., the Great Terror will not grieve them. ﴿Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding eternally therein as a reward for what they used to do﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 14]

The commentary on the verse: Allah's words:

﴿We have enjoined upon man goodness to his parents. His mother bore him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship, and his carrying and weaning take thirty months, until when he reaches his maturity and reaches forty years, he says, "My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your blessing which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to do righteousness that pleases You. And make righteous for me my offspring. Indeed, I have repented to You, and indeed, I am of the Muslims."﴾

﴿We have enjoined upon man goodness to his parents﴾ It is also read as "ḥusnan" (kindness). This is a preface for those who disobeyed and defied their parents in the matter of faith, as mentioned in His words: ﴿And one who says to his parents﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 17], and so on.

﴿His mother bore him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship﴾ That is, with hardship (kurh), or a pregnancy that involved hardship, and kurh means difficulty. ﴿And his carrying and weaning﴾ That is, his carrying as a fetus in her womb and his weaning from breastfeeding: ﴿thirty months﴾ That is, they pass for her with the suffering of hardships and the enduring of difficulties on his account, which necessitates for the mother greater care and firm attentiveness. It cannot be said that three months remain, because the limit of breastfeeding is two years. We say: the two years are the limit for one who wishes to complete the full term, but otherwise the basic period is less than them, as His words indicate: ﴿two complete years for whoever wishes to complete the nursing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 233]. And even if it is granted that the two years are its limit, then the verse relies on the round numbers and omits the fractions, following their custom in that, as they mentioned in the hadith of Anas concerning the death of the Prophet (ﷺ) at the age of sixty, although the correct view is that he died at sixty-three, as explained in the commentary on the Shama'il. They said: the narrator of the first report mentioned only the round numbers and omitted the fractions. The secret of this is the intention to mention what is important and what suffices for the subject of the speech, not the precise counting of the numbers and the exact calculation of figures.

Ibn Kathir said: Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) used this verse together with the one in Luqman: ﴿and his weaning is in two years﴾ [Luqman: 14], and the words of the Blessed and Exalted: ﴿And mothers nurse their children two complete years for whoever wishes to complete the nursing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 233], to show that the minimum period of pregnancy is six months. This is a strong and sound deduction, and Uthman and a group of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them all) agreed with him on it.

﴿Until when he reaches his maturity﴾ That is, his strength and intellect become firm. ﴿And reaches forty years, he says, "My Lord, enable me"﴾ That is, inspire me: ﴿to be grateful for Your blessing which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents﴾ That is, by guidance to monotheism, acting in obedience to You, and other than that. ﴿And to do righteousness that pleases You, and make righteous for me my offspring﴾ That is, make the righteousness flow in my offspring and firmly established among them. ﴿Indeed, I have repented to You﴾ That is, from my sins that have passed from me. ﴿And indeed, I am of the Muslims﴾ That is, those who submit to Your command and prohibition, and who yield to Your judgment.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[17] ﴿And he who says to his parents, "Uff to you both! Do you promise me that I will be brought forth, when generations have passed before me?" While they both call upon God for help, [saying], "Woe to you! Believe, for the promise of God is true." But he says, "This is not but the legends of the former peoples."﴾

Or the meaning is: they ask that God aid him with success, until he returns from what he is upon: ﴿"Woe to you! Believe"﴾ — i.e., affirm the promise of God, and acknowledge that you will be resurrected after your death. And ﴿"Woe to you"﴾ originally means a supplication for destruction, but it is put in the place of urging toward an action or an abandonment, to indicate that whoever commits it deserves to have destruction sought for him; so when he hears that, he leaves what he is in and takes what benefits him: ﴿"For the promise of God is true"﴾ — i.e., His promise to His creation, that He will raise them from their graves to the place of reckoning, to recompense them for their deeds, is true, without doubt: ﴿"But he says"﴾ — i.e., answering his parents, rejecting their counsel to them, and denying the promise of God: ﴿"This is not but the legends of the former peoples"﴾ — i.e., their falsehoods which they wrote down.

[18] ﴿Those are the ones against whom the word has come into effect, among nations that passed away before them of jinn and mankind. Indeed, they were losers.﴾

﴿Those are the ones against whom the word has come into effect﴾, i.e., the divine word, which is the punishment: ﴿among nations that passed away before them of jinn and mankind﴾, i.e., those who denied the messengers of God and defied His command. ﴿Indeed, they were losers﴾, i.e., by exchanging guidance for misguidance, and the enduring for the perishing.

**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 46, verse 19:**

**The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:**

[19] ﴿And for each there are degrees according to what they did, and that He may fully pay them their deeds, and they will not be wronged.﴾

﴿For each﴾ means: of the two groups. ﴿Degrees according to what they did﴾ means: levels of recompense for what they did of good and evil. ﴿That He may fully pay them their deeds﴾ means: their recompense. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾ means: no reward is diminished, and no punishment is increased.

**Note (tanbih):**

Ibn Jarir narrated from Ibn Abbas that this verse was revealed concerning a son of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from al-Suddi, who said: It was revealed concerning Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr. He said to his two parents, and they were Abu Bakr and Umm Ruman, and they had both embraced Islam while he refused to embrace it. They kept urging him to accept Islam, but he would reject them, deny them, and say: "Where is so-and-so, and where is so-and-so?" meaning the elders of Quraysh who had died. Then he embraced Islam afterwards, and his Islam was good. So his repentance was revealed in this verse: ﴿And for each there are degrees according to what they did.﴾

The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said: However, Aisha's denial that it was revealed concerning Abd al-Rahman and his household is stronger in its chain of transmission and more worthy of acceptance. This is what al-Bukhari, al-Isma'ili, al-Nasa'i and Abu Ya'la narrated: "Marwan was the governor of Medina. Mu'awiya wanted to appoint Yazid as successor, so he wrote to Marwan about it. Marwan gathered the people and addressed them, mentioning Yazid and calling them to pledge allegiance to him. He said: Indeed Allah has shown the Commander of the Believers a good opinion regarding Yazid, and if he appoints him as successor, then Abu Bakr and Umar both appointed successors. Abd al-Rahman said: This is nothing but Heraclian (monarchy)! Marwan said: It is the sunnah of Abu Bakr and Umar. Abd al-Rahman said: Heraclian! By Allah, Abu Bakr did not appoint it for any of his sons or for any of his household, and Mu'awiya only did it out of honor for his son! Marwan said: Seize him. He entered the house of Aisha, and they could not reach him. Marwan said: This is the one concerning whom Allah revealed: ﴿And the one who said to his parents, 'Uff to you both! Do you promise me...﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 17]. Aisha said from behind the screen: Allah did not reveal anything about us of the Qur'an, except that Allah revealed my innocence. And if you wished, I could name the one concerning whom it was revealed, but the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed the father of Marwan, and Marwan was in his loins."

Among the things that support this is that: those upon whom the word has come into effect are those who will remain forever in the Fire in the knowledge of Allah, the Exalted, and Abd al-Rahman was one of the most virtuous of the Muslims and their leaders. Some have tried to reconcile this by saying that it occurred from him before his Islam, and then he embraced Islam after that. It is well known that Islam wipes out what came before it, and that the meaning of the threat in the verse applies only to those who persist in it and do not give it up. This is because of the abundance of what has come concerning pardon for those who repent. Many severe threats were revealed at the beginning of the mission, countless verses, and all of them condemn those who were polytheists at that time. No one has said that they include those people after their belief, or that they contain anything that diminishes their status and makes them a target for criticism. But Marwan could find no response to what was thrust at him except clamor, and he distracted the people from his falsehood with a tune that delights the ignorant and a saying that the rabble chew over, and they are the ones he cared about. May Allah have mercy on Abd al-Rahman! He quenched the thirst and proclaimed the truth, while having no supporter or helper. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Qutayba said in (al-Ma'arif): Four men saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in succession: Abu Quhafa, his son Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him), his son Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, and his son Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman.

He also said: It has been said: Abd al-Rahman was among the best of Quraysh, and his kunya was Abu Muhammad. He had descendants in Medina, and they were not numerous. He died suddenly in the year fifty-three, at a mountain near Mecca. Aisha brought him into the Haram, buried him, and freed a slave on his behalf. End of quote.

In Damascus, in the cemetery of Bab al-Faradis, called al-Dahdah, there is a shrine that is said to be that of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, but it is falsely attributed to him. How many are the false attributions at shrines, as one knows who investigates the dates of death carefully.

﴿So when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, they said, "This is a cloud bringing us rain." The commentary on His words, exalted is He:

[26] ﴿And We had established them in that wherein We have not established you, and We gave them hearing and sight and hearts; but their hearing and their sight and their hearts availed them nothing at all, since they used to deny the signs of Allah; and there encompassed them that which they used to mock.﴾

﴿And We had established them in that wherein We have not established you﴾: that is, We established ʿAd, and We gave them abundance of wealth and strength of bodies, in that wherein We have not established you of the world. Here "in" (in) is a negation particle, preferred over (ma) so as not to produce a heavy, quasi-repetitive effect. It has also been said that "in" is a conditional particle whose answer is omitted, the sense being: "And We had established them in that which, if We had established you in it, your transgression would have been greater." It has also been said that it is a relative-supplementary particle, as in the verse of the poet:

"A man hopes for what he does not see, and the calamities intervene between him and his nearest hope."

Al-Zamakhshari said: "The first interpretation is the correct one. This construction occurs in more than one verse of the Qur'an: ﴿They were better in furnishings and in appearance﴾ [Maryam: 74], and ﴿They were more numerous than them and mightier in strength and in monuments﴾ [Ghafir: 82]. It is more eloquent in rebuke and more effective in urging reflection."

Al-Nasir said: "Set apart for this group is His words, exalted is He: ﴿And they said, 'Who is mightier than us in strength?' Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is mightier than them in strength?﴾ [Fussilat: 15], and His words: ﴿We had established them in the earth as We have not established you﴾ [al-An'am: 6]." That is, the basic principle is the agreement of meanings in the verses that relate one account, together with the soundness of the omission and addition involved in it.

﴿And We gave them hearing and sight and hearts﴾: al-Tabari said: that is, We gave them hearing by which they would hear the admonitions of their Lord, sight by which they would see the proofs of Allah, and hearts by which they would understand what harms and benefits them. ﴿But their hearing and their sight and their hearts availed them nothing at all﴾: that is, because they did not use them for what they were created for, but for the opposite of it. ﴿Since they used to deny the signs of Allah, and there encompassed them that which they used to mock﴾: that is, the punishment.

Al-Tabari said: This is a threat from Allah, mighty and majestic is His praise, to the Quraysh. He is saying to them: Beware lest there befall you of the punishment, because of your disbelief in Allah and your denial of His messengers, what befell ʿAd, and hasten to repentance before the vengeance.

A subtle point:

Al-Shihab said: He used the singular "hearing" in the text and the plural for the others, because the thing perceived by it is one—namely sounds—while the objects perceived by the others are multiple; and because "hearing" is in origin a verbal noun; and also because what they heard from the messengers was one and the same.

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted:

[27] ﴿And We had certainly destroyed what is around you of the towns, and We had diversified the signs that they might return.﴾

﴿And We had certainly destroyed what is around you﴾ — that is, what is around your town, O people of Makkah — ﴿of the towns﴾, such as the land of Thamud, the land of Sodom, Ma'rib and the like. We warned their people with punishments (al-muthulat), We ruined their dwellings, and We left them ruined upon their roofs. ﴿And We diversified the signs﴾ — that is, We admonished them with various kinds of admonitions and showed them many kinds of proofs. ﴿That they might return﴾ — that is, from disbelief in Allah and His messengers. Al-Tabari said: In the speech there is something omitted, its mention dropped because the context points to it, and it is: "But they refused except to persist in their disbelief and to persevere in their error, so We destroyed them, and none of Our might could help them."

The discussion of the words of His Exalted saying:

[28] ﴿Why then did those whom they had taken as gods besides Allah, as a means of nearness, not help them? Rather they vanished from them. That was their falsehood, and what they used to fabricate.﴾

﴿Why then did those whom they had taken as gods besides Allah, as a means of nearness, not help them?﴾ That is: why did not the idols that those nations of the past, whom We destroyed before them, had taken as objects of worship, as a means by which they drew near—so they claimed—to their Lord, help them when Our punishment came upon them, rescuing them from Our chastisement, if those idols were indeed interceding for them with their Lord, as they said: ﴿These are our intercessors with Allah﴾ [Yunus: 18].

﴿Rather they vanished from them﴾ That is: they were absent from giving them help, and they were unable to be sought for aid, just as one cannot seek help from one who has gone astray. In ﴿vanished﴾ there is a subsequent (tab'iyyah) metaphor (isti'arah). ﴿That was their falsehood﴾ That is: the loss of their gods from them, and the failure of those gods to help them, following upon their falsehood, which was their taking those idols as gods. ﴿And what they used to fabricate﴾ That is: and following upon their fabrication that those idols were their intercessors.

On the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[29–32] ﴿And when We turned towards you a group of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an. When they attended it, they said, "Be silent." When they attended it, they said, "Be silent"﴾, meaning: so that reflection and contemplation could be completed. ﴿And when it was concluded﴾, meaning: when he had finished reciting it, and its effect upon them was complete, they wished to convey its effect [to others], therefore: ﴿they returned﴾, meaning: they went back ﴿to their people as warners﴾, meaning: warning them against the error in which they were. ﴿They said, "O our people, we have heard a Book revealed after Moses"﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 30], meaning: one whose greatness is agreed upon. That is: and we have known its truthfulness because it is ﴿confirming what came before it﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 30], meaning: of all these earlier books, and it has been given preference over them in that it ﴿guides to the truth﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 30], meaning: to knowledge of realities, ﴿and to a straight path﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 30], meaning: without crookedness, which is Islam.

[p. 5358] Ibn Kathir said: That is, it guides to the truth in belief and in reports, and to a straight path in deeds. The Qur'an comprises two things: information (khabar) and command (talab). Its information is truthful, and its command is just, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice﴾ [al-An'am: 115]. He, Exalted is He, also said: ﴿He it is who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth﴾ [al-Fath: 28]. So guidance is beneficial knowledge, and the religion of truth is righteous action. Thus the jinn said: ﴿guides to the truth﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 30] in matters of belief, and ﴿to a straight path﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 30], that is, in practical matters. ﴿O our people, respond to the caller of Allah﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 31], that is, the Messenger of Allah, Muhammad, in what he calls you to of obedience to Allah. ﴿And believe in him; He will forgive you some of your sins and protect you from a painful punishment﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 31]. ﴿And whoever does not respond to the caller of Allah will not escape [Allah] on earth﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 32], that is, he cannot escape his Lord by fleeing when He wills to punish him, for he is within His grasp and authority wherever he turns. ﴿And he will have no protectors besides Him﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 32], that is, helpers who would defend him against Allah if He punishes him. ﴿Those are in clear error﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 32], that is, they have taken a path other than uprightness.

Remarks:

The first: Imam Muslim narrated from Alqamah, who said: "I asked Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him: 'Was anyone among you present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the night of the jinn?' He said: 'No. But we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one night and we lost him. We searched for him in the valleys and the mountain paths, and it was said: he has been carried off, or he has been seized! He said: So we spent the worst night any people have spent. When we rose in the morning, behold, he came from the direction of Hira'. We said: O Messenger of Allah! We lost you, we searched for you and did not find you, so we spent the worst night any people have spent. He said: "The caller of the jinn came to me, so I went with them and recited the Qur'an to them." He said: Then he set out with us and showed us their traces.'"

Imam Ahmad narrated from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "The jinn used to eavesdrop on the revelation [wahy], and they would hear a word and add ten to it. What they heard was true, and what they added was false. Before that, shooting stars were not hurled at them. But when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sent, whenever one of them went to his seat [in the heavens] he would be struck by a flaming meteor that burned whatever it hit. So they complained of this to Iblis, who said: 'This is nothing but some new matter that has occurred.' He then dispatched his troops, and found the Prophet ﷺ praying between two hills of a palm grove. They came to him and informed him, and he said: 'This is the new event that has happened on earth.'" At-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa'i narrated it in the books of tafsir of their Sunan. Likewise al-Hasan al-Basri said: he ﷺ was not aware of their matter until Allah revealed to him the news of them.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi the story of the Prophet's ﷺ departure to Ta'if, his calling them to Allah, the Most High, and their refusal of him. He related the story at length, then said: When he turned away from them, he spent the night at Nakhla, and he recited the Qur'an that night, and the jinn of Nasibin heard it. Ibn Kathir said: This is authentic, but his statement that the jinn's listening took place that night is open to question, for the jinn's listening was at the beginning of the revelation, as the hadith of Ibn Abbas mentioned above indicates. His departure to Ta'if was after the death of his uncle, and that was one or two years before the Hijrah, as Ibn Ishaq and others have established.

Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "They descended upon the Prophet ﷺ while he was reciting the Qur'an in the hollow of Nakhla. When they heard it, they said: 'Be silent!' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: ﴿And when We turned towards you a group of the jinn﴾, the verse." Ibn Kathir said: This, together with the first report from Ibn Abbas, may he be pleased with them both, implies that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was not aware of their presence on this occasion; they only listened to his recitation and then returned to their people. Afterwards they came to him in successive delegations, one group after another and one company after another.

[p. 5360] As for what al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated from Ma'n ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said: "I heard my father say: I asked Masruq: 'Who informed the Prophet ﷺ on the night they listened to the Qur'an?' He said: 'Your father, that is Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, told me that a tree informed him of them.'" It is possible that this refers to the first occasion, and that it is an affirmation which takes precedence over Ibn Abbas's negation. It is also possible that it refers to the first occasion, but that he was not aware of them while they were listening, until the tree informed him of their gathering. And it is possible that this refers to one of the later occasions. And Allah knows best.

The hafiz al-Bayhaqi said: What Ibn Abbas related is only the first time the jinn heard the recitation of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and learned of his condition; at that time he did not recite to them and did not see them. Then after that, the caller of the jinn came to him, and he recited the Qur'an to them and called them to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated.

Ibn Kathir then said: As for Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, he was not with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during his address to the jinn and his calling them, but was far from him, and no one went out with the Prophet ﷺ except him. Even so, he did not witness the address itself. This is al-Bayhaqi's view. It is possible that on the first occasion he went out to them, Ibn Mas'ud and others were not with him ﷺ, as the apparent context of the first narration through Imam Muslim indicates. Then afterwards he went out with him on another night, and Allah knows best, as Ibn Abi Hatim narrated in his tafsir on ﴿Say: It has been revealed to me﴾ [al-Jinn: 1] from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abd al-Aziz ibn Umar said: As for the jinn who met him at Nakhla, they were the jinn of Nineveh, and as for the jinn who met him in Makkah, they were the jinn of Nasibin.

Al-Bayhaqi interpreted the statement "we spent the worst night" as referring to someone other than Ibn Mas'ud, namely someone who was not aware of the Prophet's ﷺ going out to the jinn. This is possible, though a remote interpretation. [p. 5361] In sum, there has been transmitted what indicates that this occurred repeatedly. It has also been transmitted from Ibn Abbas, through a sound chain cited by Ibn Jarir on this verse, something other than what was transmitted from him earlier: he said: They were seven men from the people of Nasibin, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made them messengers to their people. This indicates that he narrated both accounts. Abu Hamzah al-Thumali mentioned that this tribe of the jinn were the most numerous of the jinn and the noblest in lineage. It is also reported from Ibn Mas'ud that they were nine. It is said that they were fifteen, it is reported as sixty, and it is reported as three hundred. From Ikrimah it is reported that they were twelve thousand. Ibn Kathir said: Perhaps this difference is evidence of their repeated delegations to him ﷺ.

Among what indicates this is what al-Bukhari recorded in his Sahih: that Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "I never heard Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, say about anything: 'I think it is thus,' except that it turned out as he thought. While Umar ibn al-Khattab was sitting, a handsome man passed by him, and he said: 'My assumption has been mistaken, or this man is upon his religion of the Jahiliyyah, or he was their soothsayer. Bring the man to me.' He was summoned, and [Umar] said to him what he had said. [The man] said: 'I have never seen a Muslim man confronted with the like of what you have just done today.' [Umar] said: 'I adjure you to tell me [the truth]!'

He said: 'I was their soothsayer in the Jahiliyyah.' [Umar] said: 'What is the most astonishing thing your jinn companion (ra'iy) brought you?' He said: 'One day while I was in the market, she came to me, and I could see fear in her. She said: Have you not seen the jinn and their abasement, their despair after their reversal, and their clinging to the mares and their saddle-cloths?' Umar said: 'She spoke the truth! While I was sleeping near their idols, a man came with a calf and slaughtered it, and a shouter cried out with it, a shout the like of which I had never heard, saying: "O Jalih! A successful matter, an eloquent man, saying: There is no god but Allah!" The people leapt up, and I said: I will not leave until I know what lies behind this. Then he called out again: "O Jalih! A successful matter, an eloquent man, saying: There is no god but Allah!" I got up, and we had not yet gone far before it was said: This is a Prophet.'" This is the wording of al-Bukhari. Al-Bayhaqi also narrated it with similar wording from the hadith of Ibn Wahb.

Then he said: The apparent meaning of this report gives the impression that Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, himself heard the shouter crying out from the calf that had been slaughtered. [p. 5362] Indeed, this is explicit in a weak report from Umar, may Allah be pleased with him. But the rest of the reports indicate that it was this soothsayer who reported it from his own seeing and hearing. And Allah knows best.

This man was Sawad ibn Qarib. Al-Bayhaqi said: Sawad ibn Qarib is likely to be the soothsayer whose name is not mentioned in the sound hadith. Then he narrated with his chain from al-Bara', who said: "While Umar ibn al-Khattab was delivering a sermon to the people from the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: 'O people! Is Sawad ibn Qarib among you?' No one answered him that year. When the following year came, he said: 'O people! Is Sawad ibn Qarib among you?' I said: 'O Commander of the Faithful! Who is Sawad ibn Qarib?' Umar said to him: 'Sawad ibn Qarib's beginning in Islam was something astonishing!' He said: While we were in this state, Sawad ibn Qarib appeared. Umar said to him: 'O Sawad! Tell us how your beginning in Islam came about.' Sawad said: 'I was staying in India, and I had a companion (ra'iy) from among the jinn.' He said: 'One night while I was sleeping, it came to me in my dream and said: Rise, understand and reflect, if you are able to reflect! A messenger has been sent from Lu'ayy ibn Ghalib.' Then it began to recite:

I marvelled at the jinn and their pursuit, and their driving of camels with their saddle-cloths.
They yearn towards Makkah seeking guidance; the best of the jinn are not like their wretched ones.
So rise to the chosen one of Hashim, and let your eyes be turned towards its head.

He said: Then it roused me and frightened me and said: 'O Sawad ibn Qarib! Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has sent a prophet, so rise towards him and you will be guided and rightly directed.' When it was the second night, it came to me, roused me, and then began to recite:

I marvelled at the jinn and their pursuit, and their driving of camels by their saddle-pads.
They yearn towards Makkah seeking guidance; their two forefeet are not like their tails.
So rise to the chosen one of Hashim, and let your eyes be turned towards its [forehead].

When it was the third night, it came to me, roused me, and then said:

I marvelled at the jinn and their knowledge [of the unseen], and their driving of camels by their packs.
They yearn towards Makkah seeking guidance; those with evil are not like the good among them.
So rise to the chosen one of Hashim; the believing jinn are not like their unbelievers.

[p. 5363] He said: When he heard it repeated night after night, the love of Islam entered my heart, by the decree of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, to the extent that Allah willed. He said: I went to my saddlebag, tied it tightly on my mount, and did not untie one cord or tie another until I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He was in Madinah, meaning Makkah, and the people around him were like the mane of a horse. When the Prophet ﷺ saw me, he said: "Welcome to you, O Sawad ibn Qarib. We know what has brought you." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have composed a poem. Let me recite it to you." He ﷺ said: "Say it, O Sawad." So I said:

My companion came to me after a night and a sleep,
and in what I have tested, he was never a liar.

Three nights, each night he would say:
"A messenger from Luayy ibn Ghalib has come to you."

So I hitched up my izar above my calves,
and the swift, strong she-camel carried me through the desert plains.

I bear witness that Allah, there is no lord but Him,
and that you are trusted over every unseen matter.

And that you are the nearest of the messengers in intercession
to Allah, O son of the most noble and the best.

So command us with what comes to you, O best of messengers,
even if what has come is the greying of the forelocks.

Be for me an intercessor on the day when no one has intercession
besides you, to suffice for Sawad ibn Qarib.

He said: The Prophet ﷺ laughed until his back teeth were visible, and said to me: "You have prospered, O Sawad!" Then Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said to him: "Does your companion still come to you now?" He said: "Since I recited the Qur'an, he has not come to me, and the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is a fine replacement for the jinn." Then al-Bayhaqi transmitted it through two other routes. The words of Ibn Kathir end here.

It has been related by Imam al-Mawardi in (A'lam al-Nubuwwah) together with similar reports, in the sixteenth chapter, on the calls of the jinn. Then he said: Even if these calls are khabar al-ahad (solitary reports) from one whose person is not seen and whose testimony is not decisive, their departure from the ordinary habit is a warning, and their effect on souls is a glad tiding, and the listeners have accepted them. The acceptance of reports confirms their soundness and supports their proof. If it is said: If the calls of the jinn are among the signs of prophethood, [p. 5364] then it could also be a proof for the validity of kahanah (soothsaying), then there are two answers to this:

The first: the signs of prophethood are other than these; rather, these are among its heralds, and he distinguished between a sign (dalalah) and a glad tiding (bisharah) by way of information.

The second: soothsaying concerns the hidden, while glad tidings concern a specific matter; the observed is known, and the unseen is imagined. The words of al-Mawardi end here.

The second point of caution:

Al-Mawardi said: Regarding the turning away (sarf) of the jinn mentioned in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when We turned towards you a group of the jinn listening to the Qur'an﴾, there are two interpretations:

The first: they were turned away from eavesdropping on the heaven by the hurling of shooting stars, and they were not turned away from it after Jesus except after the sending of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So they said: "This event in the heaven is only for an event on the earth," and they imagined in it the renewal of prophethood. So they traversed the earth until they came upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the valley of Makkah, as he was heading to Ukaz and was performing the dawn prayer. They listened to the Qur'an, saw how he prayed, and his companions followed him. Thus they knew that this was for this event, and they were turned away from eavesdropping by the hurling of meteors. This is the view of Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him.

I say: According to this view, the (ila) in (ilayka) means the same as the lam of causation. It is mentioned in (al-Mughni) that it may come synonymous with the lam, as in: "and the matter is to you." But this is strained and remote, because it is far from what the context of the rest of the verse requires.

Then al-Mawardi said: [p. 5365] Ikrimah related that the surah he used to recite was ﴿Recite in the name of your Lord who created﴾ [al-Alaq: 1]. I say: It will come later, traced back to the Prophet through Jabir, that it was Surat al-Rahman.

Then al-Mawardi said:

The second interpretation: they were turned away from their lands by divine guidance, through Allah's grace, until they came to the Prophet of Allah in the valley of Nakhlah. Then Jibril descended to him with this verse, informed him of the coming of the jinn, and commanded him to go out to them. He went out with Ibn Masud, until he came to al-Hajun. Ibn Masud said: "He drew a line for me and said: Do not cross it."

According to the first interpretation, he did not know of them until they came to him. According to the second interpretation, Jibril informed him before their coming. The scholars differed over whether he saw them and recited to them. Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not see them and did not recite to them; rather, they heard his recitation when they passed by him while he was praying. Ibn Masud related that he saw them and recited the Qur'an to them.

I say: What Ibn Kathir has mentioned earlier is sufficient.

Then al-Mawardi said: Regarding His saying ﴿When they attended it, they said: Be silent﴾, there are two interpretations:

The first: when they attended his recitation of the Qur'an, they said: "Be silent to listen to it."

The second: when they attended the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they said: "Be silent to listen to his words." The words of al-Mawardi end here.

Ibn Kathir said: This, that is their saying "Be silent," is a mark of good manners on their part. Al-Bayhaqi related from Jabir, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited Surat al-Rahman until he finished it, then said: 'Why do I see you silent? The jinn were better than you in response. Every time I recited to them this verse: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾, they would say: "Nor do we deny any of Your favours, our Lord; to You be praise."'" It was also transmitted by al-Tirmidhi, who said: "We do not know it except from the hadith of al-Walid ibn Muslim from Zuhayr."

The third point: His saying, the Exalted, ﴿O our people, respond to the caller of Allah﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 31] indicates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sent generally to both mankind and the jinn.

[p. 5366] Ibn Kathir said: Because he called the jinn to Allah, and recited to them the surah in which there is address to both groups, their obligations, promises, and threats, and that is Surat al-Rahman. This is why He said: ﴿Respond to the caller of Allah and believe in Him﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 31]. Al-Mawardi said: The scholars have not disagreed that it is permissible for Allah to send a messenger from mankind to them, but they differed over the permissibility of a messenger from among them. Some permitted it, based on the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you?﴾ [al-An'am: 130], while others forbade it. This is the view of those who made them the offspring of Iblis, and they interpreted His saying ﴿Did there not come to you messengers from among you?﴾ [al-An'am: 130] as referring to those who, when they heard the Qur'an, turned back to their people as warners. The words of al-Mawardi end here.

I say: A parallel to this is the naming of the messengers of Jesus, peace be upon him, as "messengers" in the verse ﴿When We sent to them two﴾ [Ya-Sin: 14].

The fourth point: Those scholars who held that believing jinn do not enter Paradise have used as evidence His saying ﴿He will forgive you of your sins and protect you from a painful punishment﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 31]. They said: the reward of their righteous ones is only that they be protected from the punishment of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection; for if they had a reward for faith higher than this, it would have been mentioned.

Al-Mawardi said: As for their disbelievers, they will enter the Fire. As for their believers, they differed over whether they enter Paradise as a reward for their faith. Al-Dahhak said: "Whoever permits that their messengers were from among them, they will enter Paradise." Sufyan related from Layth that they will be rewarded for faith by being protected from the Fire, and then it will be said to them: "Be dust like the beasts." The words of al-Mawardi end here.

The truth, as Ibn Kathir said, is that their believer is like the believer among mankind; they enter Paradise, as is the view of a group of the early generations (al-salaf). Some of them have used as evidence for this His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Neither man nor jinn has touched them before them﴾ [al-Rahman: 74]. But there is room for scrutiny in this argument. A better proof is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿But for whoever fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾ [al-Rahman: 46], ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾ [al-Rahman: 47]. He, the Exalted, has bestowed His favour upon both the two weighty groups by making the reward of their good-doers Paradise. The jinn responded to this verse with verbal gratitude more eloquently than mankind, saying: "Nor do we deny any of Your favours, our Lord; to You be praise." So He, the Exalted, would not bestow favour upon them with a reward that they do not attain.

Also, if He repays their disbelievers with the Fire, which is a station of justice, then all the more He repays their believers with Paradise, which is a station of grace, by way of a stronger and more fitting argument. Among what also indicates the generality of this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have the Gardens of Paradise as a lodging﴾ [al-Kahf: 107], and what resembles that of verses. What they have mentioned here of reward for faith, namely the expiation of sins and protection from the painful punishment, necessarily entails entering Paradise, because in the Hereafter there is nothing but Paradise or the Fire. Whoever is protected from the Fire enters Paradise without doubt. No explicit text or apparent evidence from the Lawgiver has reached us stating that believing jinn do not enter Paradise even if they are protected from the Fire; and if it were authentic, we would adopt it. And Allah knows best. Here is Noah, peace be upon him, saying to his people: ﴿He will forgive you of your sins and delay you until a specified term﴾ [Nuh: 4]. There is no disagreement that the believers among his people are in Paradise; so likewise these. Strange views have been reported about them. From Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz: they will not enter the center of Paradise, but will be around its outskirts, its surroundings, and its edges.

Some people claimed that in Paradise the children of Adam will see them, while they will not see the children of Adam, the reverse of their state in the worldly abode. Some people said: they do not eat or drink in Paradise, but they are inspired with glorification, praise, and sanctification in place of food and drink, like the angels, because they are of their kind. All these views are open to scrutiny and have no proof. The words of al-Mawardi end here.

The fifth point: It has been said: the secret of the partial (tab'id) in His saying ﴿of your sins﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 31] is that there is a punishment that is not forgiven by faith, such as the sins of injustice (al-mazalim), that is, the rights of people. But there is room for scrutiny in this, because if a combatant (harbi) plunders protected property and sheds sanctified blood, and then his Islam is good, Islam erases the sin of what came before him without any problem. [p. 5368] It is said: He did not promise forgiveness to the disbeliever on condition of faith in the Book of Allah except in a partial form. The secret of this is that the station of the disbeliever is constriction (qabd), not expansion (bast), and therefore his hope is not expanded as it is in the case of the believer. This was related by al-Nasir.

The sixth point: Ibn Kathir said: In their claim to their people they combined encouragement and warning, and for this reason it had an effect on many of them, and they came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in delegations, delegation after delegation, as has already been explained.

The seventh point: Al-Mawardi said: The jinn belong to the speaking, discerning world. They eat, marry, reproduce, and die. Their persons are veiled from sight, although they are distinguished by actions and traces; but Allah singles out whom He wills to see them. Mankind came to know them from the divine books and from what they imagined of their hidden traces.

Al-Qashani said: The jinn are earthly souls embodied in subtle bodies composed of subtle elements. The sages of Persia named them "the suspended forms." Because they are earthly, embodied in elemental bodies, and share this with mankind, both are called "the two weighty ones" (al-thaqalan). Just as it was possible for people to challenge with the Qur'an, it was possible for them too, and the reports of them from the verifiers and others are more than can be counted, and too clear to accept interpretation. The words of al-Qashani end here.

**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 46, verses 29–32 (part 1 of 2)**

On the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[29–32] ﴿And when We turned towards you a group of the jinn, listening to the Qur'an. When they attended it, they said, "Be silent." And when it was concluded, they returned to their people as warners.﴾ ﴿They said, "O our people, we have heard a Book revealed after Moses, confirming what came before it, guiding to the truth and to a straight path."﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 30] ﴿O our people, respond to the caller of Allah and believe in him; He will forgive you some of your sins and protect you from a painful punishment.﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 31] ﴿And whoever does not respond to the caller of Allah will not escape [Allah] on earth, and he will have no protectors besides Him. Those are in clear error.﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 32]

﴿And when We turned towards you a group of the jinn﴾, meaning: We directed them to you and brought them towards you. ﴿Listening to the Qur'an. When they attended it, they said, "Be silent"﴾, meaning: so that reflection and contemplation could be completed. ﴿And when it was concluded﴾, meaning: when he had finished reciting it, and its effect upon them was complete, they wished to convey its effect [to others], therefore: ﴿they returned﴾, meaning: they went back ﴿to their people as warners﴾, meaning: warning them against the error in which they were. ﴿They said, "O our people, we have heard a Book revealed after Moses"﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 30], meaning: one whose greatness is agreed upon. That is: and we have known its truthfulness because it is ﴿confirming what came before it﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 30], meaning: of all these earlier books, and it has been given preference over them in that it ﴿guides to the truth﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 30], meaning: to knowledge of realities, ﴿and to a straight path﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 30], meaning: without crookedness, which is Islam.

[p. 5358] Ibn Kathir said: That is, it guides to the truth in belief and in reports, and to a straight path in deeds. The Qur'an comprises two things: information (khabar) and command (talab). Its information is truthful, and its command is just, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice﴾ [al-An'am: 115]. He, Exalted is He, also said: ﴿He it is who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth﴾ [al-Fath: 28]. So guidance is beneficial knowledge, and the religion of truth is righteous action. Thus the jinn said: ﴿guides to the truth﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 30] in matters of belief, and ﴿to a straight path﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 30], that is, in practical matters. ﴿O our people, respond to the caller of Allah﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 31], that is, the Messenger of Allah, Muhammad, in what he calls you to of obedience to Allah. ﴿And believe in him; He will forgive you some of your sins and protect you from a painful punishment﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 31]. ﴿And whoever does not respond to the caller of Allah will not escape [Allah] on earth﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 32], that is, he cannot escape his Lord by fleeing when He wills to punish him, for he is within His grasp and authority wherever he turns. ﴿And he will have no protectors besides Him﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 32], that is, helpers who would defend him against Allah if He punishes him. ﴿Those are in clear error﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 32], that is, they have taken a path other than uprightness.

Remarks:

The first: Imam Muslim narrated from Alqamah, who said: "I asked Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him: 'Was anyone among you present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the night of the jinn?' He said: 'No. But we were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ one night and we lost him. We searched for him in the valleys and the mountain paths, and it was said: he has been carried off, or he has been seized! He said: So we spent the worst night any people have spent. When we rose in the morning, behold, he came from the direction of Hira'. We said: O Messenger of Allah! We lost you, we searched for you and did not find you, so we spent the worst night any people have spent. He said: "The caller of the jinn came to me, so I went with them and recited the Qur'an to them." He said: Then he set out with us and showed us their traces.'"

Imam Ahmad narrated from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "The jinn used to eavesdrop on the revelation [wahy], and they would hear a word and add ten to it. What they heard was true, and what they added was false. Before that, shooting stars were not hurled at them. But when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sent, whenever one of them went to his seat [in the heavens] he would be struck by a flaming meteor that burned whatever it hit. So they complained of this to Iblis, who said: 'This is nothing but some new matter that has occurred.' He then dispatched his troops, and found the Prophet ﷺ praying between two hills of a palm grove. They came to him and informed him, and he said: 'This is the new event that has happened on earth.'" At-Tirmidhi and an-Nasa'i narrated it in the books of tafsir of their Sunan. Likewise al-Hasan al-Basri said: he ﷺ was not aware of their matter until Allah revealed to him the news of them.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi the story of the Prophet's ﷺ departure to Ta'if, his calling them to Allah, the Most High, and their refusal of him. He related the story at length, then said: When he turned away from them, he spent the night at Nakhla, and he recited the Qur'an that night, and the jinn of Nasibin heard it. Ibn Kathir said: This is authentic, but his statement that the jinn's listening took place that night is open to question, for the jinn's listening was at the beginning of the revelation, as the hadith of Ibn Abbas mentioned above indicates. His departure to Ta'if was after the death of his uncle, and that was one or two years before the Hijrah, as Ibn Ishaq and others have established.

Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "They descended upon the Prophet ﷺ while he was reciting the Qur'an in the hollow of Nakhla. When they heard it, they said: 'Be silent!' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: ﴿And when We turned towards you a group of the jinn﴾, the verse." Ibn Kathir said: This, together with the first report from Ibn Abbas, may he be pleased with them both, implies that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was not aware of their presence on this occasion; they only listened to his recitation and then returned to their people. Afterwards they came to him in successive delegations, one group after another and one company after another.

[p. 5360] As for what al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated from Ma'n ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said: "I heard my father say: I asked Masruq: 'Who informed the Prophet ﷺ on the night they listened to the Qur'an?' He said: 'Your father, that is Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, told me that a tree informed him of them.'" It is possible that this refers to the first occasion, and that it is an affirmation which takes precedence over Ibn Abbas's negation. It is also possible that it refers to the first occasion, but that he was not aware of them while they were listening, until the tree informed him of their gathering. And it is possible that this refers to one of the later occasions. And Allah knows best.

The hafiz al-Bayhaqi said: What Ibn Abbas related is only the first time the jinn heard the recitation of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and learned of his condition; at that time he did not recite to them and did not see them. Then after that, the caller of the jinn came to him, and he recited the Qur'an to them and called them to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated.

Ibn Kathir then said: As for Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, he was not with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during his address to the jinn and his calling them, but was far from him, and no one went out with the Prophet ﷺ except him. Even so, he did not witness the address itself. This is al-Bayhaqi's view. It is possible that on the first occasion he went out to them, Ibn Mas'ud and others were not with him ﷺ, as the apparent context of the first narration through Imam Muslim indicates. Then afterwards he went out with him on another night, and Allah knows best, as Ibn Abi Hatim narrated in his tafsir on ﴿Say: It has been revealed to me﴾ [al-Jinn: 1] from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abd al-Aziz ibn Umar said: As for the jinn who met him at Nakhla, they were the jinn of Nineveh, and as for the jinn who met him in Makkah, they were the jinn of Nasibin.

Al-Bayhaqi interpreted the statement "we spent the worst night" as referring to someone other than Ibn Mas'ud, namely someone who was not aware of the Prophet's ﷺ going out to the jinn. This is possible, though a remote interpretation. [p. 5361] In sum, there has been transmitted what indicates that this occurred repeatedly. It has also been transmitted from Ibn Abbas, through a sound chain cited by Ibn Jarir on this verse, something other than what was transmitted from him earlier: he said: They were seven men from the people of Nasibin, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made them messengers to their people. This indicates that he narrated both accounts. Abu Hamzah al-Thumali mentioned that this tribe of the jinn were the most numerous of the jinn and the noblest in lineage. It is also reported from Ibn Mas'ud that they were nine. It is said that they were fifteen, it is reported as sixty, and it is reported as three hundred. From Ikrimah it is reported that they were twelve thousand. Ibn Kathir said: Perhaps this difference is evidence of their repeated delegations to him ﷺ.

Among what indicates this is what al-Bukhari recorded in his Sahih: that Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "I never heard Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, say about anything: 'I think it is thus,' except that it turned out as he thought. While Umar ibn al-Khattab was sitting, a handsome man passed by him, and he said: 'My assumption has been mistaken, or this man is upon his religion of the Jahiliyyah, or he was their soothsayer. Bring the man to me.' He was summoned, and [Umar] said to him what he had said. [The man] said: 'I have never seen a Muslim man confronted with the like of what you have just done today.' [Umar] said: 'I adjure you to tell me [the truth]!'

He said: 'I was their soothsayer in the Jahiliyyah.' [Umar] said: 'What is the most astonishing thing your jinn companion (ra'iy) brought you?' He said: 'One day while I was in the market, she came to me, and I could see fear in her. She said: Have you not seen the jinn and their abasement, their despair after their reversal, and their clinging to the mares and their saddle-cloths?' Umar said: 'She spoke the truth! While I was sleeping near their idols, a man came with a calf and slaughtered it, and a shouter cried out with it, a shout the like of which I had never heard, saying: "O Jalih! A successful matter, an eloquent man, saying: There is no god but Allah!" The people leapt up, and I said: I will not leave until I know what lies behind this. Then he called out again: "O Jalih! A successful matter, an eloquent man, saying: There is no god but Allah!" I got up, and we had not yet gone far before it was said: This is a Prophet.'" This is the wording of al-Bukhari. Al-Bayhaqi also narrated it with similar wording from the hadith of Ibn Wahb.

Then he said: The apparent meaning of this report gives the impression that Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, himself heard the shouter crying out from the calf that had been slaughtered. [p. 5362] Indeed, this is explicit in a weak report from Umar, may Allah be pleased with him. But the rest of the reports indicate that it was this soothsayer who reported it from his own seeing and hearing. And Allah knows best.

This man was Sawad ibn Qarib. Al-Bayhaqi said: Sawad ibn Qarib is likely to be the soothsayer whose name is not mentioned in the sound hadith. Then he narrated with his chain from al-Bara', who said: "While Umar ibn al-Khattab was delivering a sermon to the people from the pulpit of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: 'O people! Is Sawad ibn Qarib among you?' No one answered him that year. When the following year came, he said: 'O people! Is Sawad ibn Qarib among you?' I said: 'O Commander of the Faithful! Who is Sawad ibn Qarib?' Umar said to him: 'Sawad ibn Qarib's beginning in Islam was something astonishing!' He said: While we were in this state, Sawad ibn Qarib appeared. Umar said to him: 'O Sawad! Tell us how your beginning in Islam came about.' Sawad said: 'I was staying in India, and I had a companion (ra'iy) from among the jinn.' He said: 'One night while I was sleeping, it came to me in my dream and said: Rise, understand and reflect, if you are able to reflect! A messenger has been sent from Lu'ayy ibn Ghalib.' Then it began to recite:

I marvelled at the jinn and their pursuit, and their driving of camels with their saddle-cloths.
They yearn towards Makkah seeking guidance; the best of the jinn are not like their wretched ones.
So rise to the chosen one of Hashim, and let your eyes be turned towards its head.

He said: Then it roused me and frightened me and said: 'O Sawad ibn Qarib! Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has sent a prophet, so rise towards him and you will be guided and rightly directed.' When it was the second night, it came to me, roused me, and then began to recite:

I marvelled at the jinn and their pursuit, and their driving of camels by their saddle-pads.
They yearn towards Makkah seeking guidance; their two forefeet are not like their tails.
So rise to the chosen one of Hashim, and let your eyes be turned towards its [forehead].

When it was the third night, it came to me, roused me, and then said:

I marvelled at the jinn and their knowledge [of the unseen], and their driving of camels by their packs.
They yearn towards Makkah seeking guidance; those with evil are not like the good among them.
So rise to the chosen one of Hashim; the believing jinn are not like their unbelievers.

[p. 5363] He said: When he heard it repeated night after night, the love of Islam entered my heart, by the decree of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, to the extent that Allah willed. He said: I went to my saddlebag, tied it tightly on my mount, and did not untie one cord or tie another until I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He was in Madinah, meaning Makkah, and the people around him were like the mane of a horse. When the Prophet ﷺ saw me, he said: "Welcome to you, O Sawad ibn Qarib. We know what has brought you." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have composed a poem. Let me recite it to you." He ﷺ said: "Say it, O Sawad." So I said:

My companion came to me after a night and a sleep,
